title: Android Studio Memory Profiler 核心工作流
key_conclusions: Android Studio Memory Profiler should be used as an evidence entry point: timeline first, then heap dump, allocation recording, class-instance inspection, and before/after replay.
Profiler heap and allocation views complement LeakCanary; Profiler finds when and what grows, while LeakCanary or MAT is needed to prove retained ownership paths.

Java heap charts do not prove fd, CursorWindow, socket, graphics, or native resource release, so resource cases still require /proc/<pid>/fd, dumpsys meminfo, StrictMode, CloseGuard, heapprofd, or similar external evidence.
A fix is acceptable only when the same scenario shows stable post-GC baseline, suspect instance counts, allocation hotspots, and all relevant resource metrics.
shallow_points: The article still uses representative profiler workflows rather than screenshots or exports from a real Android Studio profiling session.
It does not open the same HPROF in Android Studio, LeakCanary/Shark, and MAT for side-by-side retained-path comparison.
It does not validate exact Android Studio UI labels against one pinned Android Studio version.
It does not include a runnable sample app with repeatable Activity, Fragment view, allocation churn, fd, and native leak scenarios.
discovered_connections: Day 21's LeakCanary boundary becomes the central Profiler boundary: Profiler can reveal Java object and allocation symptoms, but retained ownership and resource lifetime need separate evidence.
Day 20's resource-not-closed evidence chain remains necessary when Profiler shows only a small Java wrapper while fd or native memory keeps growing.
Day 23 should deepen this by walking through HPROF records, classes, instances, references, roots, and retained objects from the same heap dump.
Day 24 should compare Android Studio heap views with MAT dominator tree and Path To GC Roots on the same dump.
Day 26 should reuse the allocation-recording workflow and expand it into object churn and call-site hotspot analysis.
suggest_future_topics: Day 23 should use a concrete HPROF-style walkthrough to explain file structure, records, class instances, references, GC roots, and retained objects.

A later sample-app article should generate reproducible profiler sessions and store before/after artifacts.
